# SRv6 on Linux: Kernel Behaviors, iproute2 Recipes and a Lab

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/linux-kernel/
Path: implementations/linux-kernel.md
Summary: SRv6 in the Linux kernel: which seg6 behaviors landed in which kernel, iproute2 recipes for encap and seg6local, a tested two-namespace lab and troubleshooting.

# SRv6 on Linux

The Linux kernel has had native SRv6 since **4.10** (February 2017; `seg6local` endpoint behaviors since 4.14) and is one of the most complete open-source SRv6 data planes. Everything is configured with **iproute2**: `seg6` routes act as headends (H.Encaps and friends), and `seg6local` routes bind local SIDs to endpoint behaviors (End, End.X, End.DT4, …). Routing daemons such as [FRRouting](https://srv6.md/implementations/frrouting/) program the same kernel objects, so what you learn here applies to FRR, SONiC hosts and container labs alike.

## Behavior Support by Kernel Version

First mainline release containing each feature, checked against the kernel git history (latest release: 7.3, October 2026). Distribution and stable kernels may carry fixes earlier; features also need a matching **iproute2**.

### Headend behaviors (`ip route ... encap seg6 mode ...`)

| RFC 8986 behavior | iproute2 mode | Kernel | Notes |
|-------------------|---------------|:------:|-------|
| H.Encaps | `encap` | **4.10** | IPv6 or IPv4 payload |
| *SRH insertion* (not in RFC 8986) | `inline` | **4.10** | Adds an SRH to an IPv6 packet in place |
| H.Encaps.L2 | `l2encap` | **4.14** | Ethernet payload |
| H.Encaps.Red | `encap.red` | **6.0** | iproute2 6.0 |
| H.Encaps.L2.Red | `l2encap.red` | **6.0** | iproute2 6.0 |
| Per-route outer source (`tunsrc`) | `... tunsrc ` | **7.1** | iproute2 7.1; overrides the per-namespace `ip sr tunsrc` |

### Endpoint behaviors (`ip -6 route ... encap seg6local action ...`)

| Behavior | Kernel | Notes |
|----------|:------:|-------|
| End | **4.14** | `seg6local` itself arrived in 4.14 |
| End.X | **4.14** | Optional `oif` for link-local next hops from 6.17 |
| End.T | **4.14** | `table N` |
| End.DX2 | **4.14** | `oif `; no VLAN variant (End.DX2V) |
| End.DX4 / End.DX6 | **4.14** | `nh4` / `nh6` |
| End.DT6 | **4.14** (`table`), **5.11** (`vrftable`) | VRF mode needs `net.vrf.strict_mode=1` |
| End.DT4 | **5.11** | `vrftable` only; needs VRF strict mode |
| End.DT46 | **5.14** | `vrftable`; needs VRF strict mode |
| End.B6 (SRH insertion) | **4.14** | `srh segs ...` |
| End.B6.Encaps | **4.14** | `srh segs ...` |
| End.BPF | **4.18** | Attach an eBPF program as the behavior |
| PSP flavor | **6.3** | End only (`flavors psp`) |
| NEXT-C-SID flavor (uSID) | **6.1** (End), **6.6** (End.X) | `flavors next-csid lblen 32 nflen 16` (defaults 32/16) |
| Per-SID counters | **5.13** | `count`; iproute2 5.14 |

### Infrastructure

| Feature | Kernel | Notes |
|---------|:------:|-------|
| SRH processing, `seg6_enabled` sysctl | **4.10** | Per interface; see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) |
| HMAC TLV, `seg6_require_hmac`, `ip sr hmac` | **4.10** | Constant-time MAC compare from 6.17 |
| `ip sr tunsrc` (per-namespace outer source) | **4.10** | Default `::` = pick from the egress interface |
| `net.ipv6.seg6_flowlabel` | **4.18** | Compute the outer flow label for encapsulated traffic |
| Netfilter hooks on seg6/seg6local | **5.15** | Off by default; `net.netfilter.nf_hooks_lwtunnel=1` |
| Post-encapsulation lookup in a chosen FIB table | **7.3** | `SEG6_IPTUNNEL_TABLE`; iproute2 support not yet in a release |

!!! warning "Not implemented in the kernel"
    End.DX2V, End.DT2U, End.DT2M, End.B6.Encaps.Red, the USP and USD flavors, REPLACE-C-SID and every [RFC 9433](https://srv6.md/rfcs/rfc9433/) mobile behavior. `End.BM`, `End.S`, `End.AS` and `End.AM` exist as names in the UAPI and in iproute2, but the kernel has no implementation behind them. For EVPN (End.DT2U/DT2M), use [FRRouting](https://srv6.md/implementations/frrouting/) with a VXLAN data plane or a vendor router. For MUP behaviors, use an eBPF data plane such as [Vinbero](https://srv6.md/implementations/vinbero/).

## iproute2 Recipes

Every command on this page was tested on kernel 6.12 with iproute2 6.9. Behavior names follow [RFC 8986](https://srv6.md/topics/network-programming/); in iproute2 they are the `action` keyword of a `seg6local` route.

### Headend: steering traffic into SRv6 (`seg6`)

```bash
# H.Encaps: IPv4 prefix into an outer IPv6 header + SRH with two segments
ip route add 198.51.100.0/24 encap seg6 mode encap \
    segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::a4 dev eth0

# H.Encaps.Red: same, but the first SID is only in the DA (SRH one entry shorter;
# with a single SID there is no SRH at all)
ip route add 198.51.101.0/24 encap seg6 mode encap.red \
    segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::a4 dev eth0

# uSID: one container carrying uN(3) uN(4) uDT4 — no SRH needed
ip route add 198.51.102.0/24 encap seg6 mode encap \
    segs fcbb:bb00:300:400:e004:: dev eth0

# SRH insertion into an existing IPv6 packet (not an RFC 8986 behavior)
ip -6 route add 2001:db8:99::/48 encap seg6 mode inline segs fc00:0:3::1 dev eth0

# H.Encaps.L2 / H.Encaps.L2.Red: frames received for this route are carried as Ethernet payload
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::12/128 encap seg6 mode l2encap segs fc00:0:4::d2 dev eth1
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::13/128 encap seg6 mode l2encap.red segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::d2 dev eth1
```

The outer source address comes from `ip sr tunsrc set ` (one per network namespace); if it is unset, the kernel picks a source address of the outgoing interface. Kernel and iproute2 7.1 add a per-route `tunsrc ` option that overrides it.

### Endpoint behaviors (`seg6local`)

```bash
# End (node SID), optionally with the PSP flavor (6.3+)
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::1/128 encap seg6local action End dev eth0
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::2/128 encap seg6local action End flavors psp dev eth0

# End.X (adjacency SID) toward a specific IPv6 next hop
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1:e001::/64 encap seg6local action End.X nh6 2001:db8:1::2 dev eth0

# End.T: next segment looked up in table 10
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::3/128 encap seg6local action End.T table 10 dev eth0

# End.DX4 / End.DX6: decapsulate and cross-connect to a next hop (per-CE VPN)
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::d4/128 encap seg6local action End.DX4 nh4 192.0.2.2 dev eth1
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::d6/128 encap seg6local action End.DX6 nh6 2001:db8:2::2 dev eth1

# End.DX2: decapsulate and send the inner Ethernet frame out of eth1
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::d2/128 encap seg6local action End.DX2 oif eth1 dev eth1

# End.B6 (SRH insertion) and End.B6.Encaps: binding SIDs for an SR policy
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::b6/128 encap seg6local action End.B6 srh segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::1 dev eth0
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::b7/128 encap seg6local action End.B6.Encaps srh segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::1 dev eth0

# Per-SID counters (read with: ip -s -6 route show fc00:0:1::c)
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::c/128 encap seg6local action End count dev eth0
```

### VRF decapsulation: End.DT4, End.DT6, End.DT46

The table-lookup behaviors deliver the inner packet into a **VRF**. Create the VRF first and enable strict mode; without it the kernel rejects any `vrftable` SID with `Error: Strict mode for VRF is disabled.`

```bash
ip link add vrf-red type vrf table 10
ip link set vrf-red up
sysctl -w net.vrf.strict_mode=1      # the sysctl appears once the vrf module is loaded

ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a4/128  encap seg6local action End.DT4  vrftable 10 dev vrf-red
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a6/128  encap seg6local action End.DT6  vrftable 10 dev vrf-red
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a46/128 encap seg6local action End.DT46 vrftable 10 dev vrf-red

# legacy End.DT6 form without a VRF device: plain table lookup
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a7/128 encap seg6local action End.DT6 table 10 dev eth0
```

### Compressed SIDs: NEXT-C-SID (uSID)

```bash
# uN: End with the NEXT-C-SID flavor (6.1+), 32-bit block + 16-bit node uSID
ip -6 route add fcbb:bb00:100::/48 encap seg6local action End \
    flavors next-csid lblen 32 nflen 16 dev eth0

# uA: End.X with NEXT-C-SID (6.6+)
ip -6 route add fcbb:bb00:100:e001::/64 encap seg6local action End.X nh6 2001:db8:1::2 \
    flavors next-csid lblen 32 nflen 16 dev eth0
```

`lblen` is the locator-block length and `nflen` the node + function length (both in bits, multiples of 8). See [uSID Compression](https://srv6.md/topics/usid-compression/) for how the destination address is shifted at each hop.

## Lab: Two Routers in Network Namespaces

A self-contained L3VPN over SRv6 between two network namespaces, `r1` and `r2`. Each has a customer VRF (table 100) with a dummy "LAN", an End.DT46 SID for the VRF, and an H.Encaps.Red route toward the other side. Static routes for the locators stand in for IS-IS. Run as root on any recent kernel:

```bash title="srv6-lab.sh"
#!/bin/sh
set -e
ip netns add r1
ip netns add r2
ip link add veth1 netns r1 type veth peer name veth2 netns r2

for r in r1 r2; do
  ip -n $r link set lo up
  ip -n $r link add vrf-cust type vrf table 100
  ip -n $r link set vrf-cust up
  ip -n $r link add cust0 type dummy
  ip -n $r link set cust0 master vrf-cust up
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.all.seg6_enabled=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.vrf.strict_mode=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.vrf-cust.rp_filter=0
done
ip netns exec r1 sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.veth1.seg6_enabled=1
ip netns exec r2 sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.veth2.seg6_enabled=1

ip -n r1 link set veth1 up
ip -n r2 link set veth2 up
ip -n r1 -6 addr add 2001:db8:12::1/64 dev veth1 nodad
ip -n r2 -6 addr add 2001:db8:12::2/64 dev veth2 nodad
ip -n r1 addr add 10.1.1.1/24 dev cust0
ip -n r2 addr add 10.2.2.2/24 dev cust0

# Locators: r1 = fc00:0:1::/48, r2 = fc00:0:2::/48
ip -n r1 -6 route add fc00:0:2::/48 via 2001:db8:12::2
ip -n r2 -6 route add fc00:0:1::/48 via 2001:db8:12::1

# Service SIDs: End.DT46 into the customer VRF
ip -n r1 -6 route add fc00:0:1::d46/128 encap seg6local action End.DT46 vrftable 100 dev vrf-cust
ip -n r2 -6 route add fc00:0:2::d46/128 encap seg6local action End.DT46 vrftable 100 dev vrf-cust

# Headend: H.Encaps.Red from the VRF toward the remote End.DT46 SID
ip -n r1 route add 10.2.2.0/24 vrf vrf-cust encap seg6 mode encap.red segs fc00:0:2::d46 dev veth1
ip -n r2 route add 10.1.1.0/24 vrf vrf-cust encap seg6 mode encap.red segs fc00:0:1::d46 dev veth2

ip netns exec r1 ping -c 3 -I vrf-cust 10.2.2.2
```

Watch the encapsulated traffic on r2 while pinging. With a single SID and `encap.red`, there is no SRH: the outer header's next header is 4 (IPv4).

```text
# ip netns exec r2 tcpdump -nvi veth2 'ip6[6] == 4'
IP6 (hlim 64, next-header IPIP (4) payload length: 84) 2001:db8:12::1 > fc00:0:2::d46:
    IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 60488, offset 0, flags [DF], proto ICMP (1), length 84)
    10.1.1.1 > 10.2.2.2: ICMP echo request, id 49, seq 1, length 64
```

Switch r1 to `mode encap` and the SRH appears, with one segment and Segments Left 0:

```text
# ip -n r1 route replace 10.2.2.0/24 vrf vrf-cust encap seg6 mode encap segs fc00:0:2::d46 dev veth1
# ip netns exec r2 tcpdump -nvi veth2 'ip6[6] == 43'
IP6 (hlim 64, next-header Routing (43) payload length: 108) 2001:db8:12::1 > fc00:0:2::d46:
    RT6 (len=2, type=4, segleft=0, last-entry=0, flags=0x0, tag=0, [0]fc00:0:2::d46)
    IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, ...) 10.1.1.1 > 10.2.2.2: ICMP echo request, id 54, seq 1, length 64
```

Clean up with `ip netns del r1; ip netns del r2`. To grow this into a multi-hop topology with IS-IS and BGP, move to [Containerlab](https://srv6.md/labs/containerlab/) with FRR.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Packets with an SRH are dropped on arrival | `seg6_enabled` is 0. The kernel uses the **lower** of the `all` value and the receiving interface's value, so both must be 1 | `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.seg6_enabled=1` and `net.ipv6.conf..seg6_enabled=1` |
| Transit node does not forward SRv6 traffic | IPv6 forwarding disabled | `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1` |
| End.DT4/End.DT46 decapsulates, but nothing reaches the VRF and no counter increments | Reverse-path filtering on the VRF device. Distributions often set `rp_filter` (1 or 2) by default; new devices inherit it, and the effective value is the max of `all` and the device | `sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf..rp_filter=0` (and `all`) — this was the one failure we hit building the lab above |
| `Error: Strict mode for VRF is disabled.` when adding End.DT4/DT6/DT46 | VRF strict mode off | `sysctl -w net.vrf.strict_mode=1` (after creating a VRF) |
| Ping from the VRF fails with `ip vrf exec` in containers | `ip vrf exec` needs cgroup BPF | Use `ping -I ` instead |
| Encapsulated packets leave with an unexpected source | No `tunsrc` set | `ip sr tunsrc set ` |
| Large packets disappear after encapsulation | Encapsulation adds 40 bytes (plus 8 + 16 × n for an SRH) | Raise the underlay MTU or lower the customer MTU |
| SRH packets dropped on an HMAC-enabled interface | `seg6_require_hmac` = 1 drops packets without a valid HMAC TLV | Configure keys with `ip sr hmac set` on both ends, or use 0 (validate only if present) / -1 (ignore HMAC) |

Useful commands:

```bash
ip -6 route show | grep seg6local           # local SIDs
ip route show vrf vrf-cust                  # encap routes in a VRF
ip -s -6 route show fc00:0:1::c             # per-SID counters (routes added with "count")
ip -6 route get fc00:0:2::d46               # which route/SID a destination hits
tcpdump -nvi eth0 'ip6 proto 43'            # packets whose first extension header is the SRH
tcpdump -nvi eth0 'ip6[6] == 4 or ip6[6] == 41'  # H.Encaps(.Red) with no SRH (IPv4 / IPv6 inside)
nstat -az | grep -i -E 'Ip6InNoRoutes|Ip6InDiscards|Ip6InHdrErrors'
sysctl -a 2>/dev/null | grep seg6           # seg6_enabled / seg6_require_hmac per interface
```

!!! tip "Filtering SRv6 in tcpdump"
    `ip6 proto 43` only matches when the SRH directly follows the IPv6 header. Reduced encapsulation with one SID has **no** SRH at all, so match the payload type (`ip6[6] == 4` for IPv4, `41` for IPv6) or the destination prefix (`dst net fc00::/16`).

## Not Yet Merged: Mobile User Plane (RFC 9433)

The kernel has **no** [RFC 9433](https://srv6.md/rfcs/rfc9433/) Mobile User Plane behaviors in any release up to 7.3. Patches from Yuya Kusakabe are under review on netdev (status as of 20 October 2026):

| Series | Posted | Status | What it adds |
|--------|--------|--------|--------------|
| net-next "seg6: add SRv6 Mobile User Plane (RFC 9433) behaviors" (7 patches) and the matching iproute2-next series | v1 3 May, v2 4 May 2026 | Changes requested; superseded | End.MAP, End.M.GTP4.E, End.M.GTP6.E, End.M.GTP6.D, End.M.GTP6.D.Di and H.M.GTP4.D |
| RFC net-next "seg6: add support for the SRv6 End.MAP behavior" + selftest | v1 10 July → **v5 2 October 2026** | **RFC, not merged** | End.MAP only: rewrites the IPv6 DA to a configured mapped SID and forwards via the FIB, under a new `seg6mobile` lightweight-tunnel encap |
| RFC iproute2-next "End.MAP behavior under seg6mobile encap" | v5 2 October 2026 | RFC, not applied | iproute2 support plus a new uapi header `seg6_mobile.h` |

After review of the all-in-one submission, the author split the work into **per-behavior series**, starting with End.MAP; the GTP-U interworking behaviors (End.M.GTP4.E and friends) would follow separately. An "RFC" posting cannot be merged as is, so End.MAP will not appear before a non-RFC version is accepted into net-next — at the earliest, the release after that. Until then, use an eBPF data plane such as [Vinbero](https://srv6.md/implementations/vinbero/) for MUP/GTP behaviors.

## Tools

- **iproute2** - `ip route ... encap seg6|seg6local`, `ip sr tunsrc`, `ip sr hmac`
- **tcpdump** / **tshark** - SRH decoding (`RT6 ... type=4`)
- **scapy** - Packet crafting with `IPv6ExtHdrSegmentRouting`
- **FRRouting** - IS-IS/BGP control plane that installs the same seg6 routes ([FRRouting](https://srv6.md/implementations/frrouting/))
- **eBPF** - `End.BPF` and XDP/TC programs for custom behaviors ([Vinbero](https://srv6.md/implementations/vinbero/), [Cilium](https://srv6.md/implementations/cilium/))

- [Network Programming](https://srv6.md/topics/network-programming/) - What each behavior does, per RFC 8986
- [Containerlab](https://srv6.md/labs/containerlab/) - Build a multi-node Linux SRv6 lab
- [FRRouting](https://srv6.md/implementations/frrouting/) - Add routing protocol support

- [Security](https://srv6.md/topics/security/#implementation-vulnerabilities) - Kernel SRv6 CVEs such as CVE-2026-23442

# SRv6 with Cilium: eBPF L3VPN for Kubernetes

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/cilium/
Path: implementations/cilium.md
Summary: SRv6 L3VPN and cloud-native networking with Cilium eBPF — connecting Kubernetes clusters to an SRv6 fabric using BGP and eBPF-accelerated data plane.

# SRv6 with Cilium (eBPF)

**Cilium** is an open-source, eBPF-based networking solution for Kubernetes that brings SRv6 into the cloud-native world. Instead of relying on the kernel's routing stack, Cilium programs eBPF maps in the kernel data path — enabling SRv6 encapsulation and decapsulation at line rate without context switching.

!!! info "Minimum version"
    SRv6 L3VPN support requires **Cilium 1.13+** (alpha). Production-ready use is recommended on **Cilium 1.15+**.

## Why Cilium + SRv6?

Traditional SRv6 implementations (Cisco, Juniper, FRRouting) live on routers. Cilium extends the SRv6 fabric **into the Kubernetes node** — each worker node becomes an SRv6 endpoint with its own locator, SIDs, and BGP session.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph K8s Cluster A
        P1[Pod] --> N1["K8s Node\n(Cilium agent\n+ eBPF SRv6)"]
    end
    subgraph SRv6 Fabric
        R1[PE Router] <-->|"BGP VPNv4/v6\nSRv6 SIDs"| N1
        R1 <-->|"IS-IS/OSPFv3"| R2[P Router]
        R2 <-->|"BGP VPNv4/v6\nSRv6 SIDs"| N2
    end
    subgraph K8s Cluster B
        N2["K8s Node\n(Cilium agent\n+ eBPF SRv6)"] --> P2[Pod]
    end
    style P1 fill:#1b5e2026,stroke:#1b5e20
    style P2 fill:#1b5e2026,stroke:#1b5e20
```

This makes each K8s node a first-class SRv6 PE — pod traffic is natively encapsulated into SRv6 by eBPF before it leaves the NIC, integrating seamlessly with a carrier-grade SRv6 underlay.

## Supported SRv6 Behaviors

| Behavior | Role in Cilium | Status |
|----------|---------------|:------:|
| `H.Encaps` | Egress: encapsulate pod traffic into SRv6 | 1.13+ |
| `End.DT4` | Ingress: decapsulate SRv6 → IPv4 VRF lookup | 1.13+ |
| `End.DT6` | Ingress: decapsulate SRv6 → IPv6 VRF lookup | 1.13+ |
| `H.Encaps.Red` | Reduced encapsulation (no SRH when single SID) | 1.15+ |

## Architecture

### How Cilium Implements SRv6 with eBPF

Cilium programs four eBPF maps per node that together implement the SRv6 data plane:

| eBPF Map | Key | Value | Purpose |
|----------|-----|-------|---------|
| `cilium_srv6_vrf` | Source IP + VRF ID | SRv6 locator | Maps pod traffic to a VRF |
| `cilium_srv6_policy` | Destination CIDR + VRF | Egress SID | Selects the SRv6 SID for encapsulation |
| `cilium_srv6_sid` | SRv6 SID | VRF table ID | Maps incoming SIDs to a local VRF for decapsulation |
| `cilium_srv6_state` | Flow state | — | Tracks active SRv6 flows for telemetry |

At **egress**, the eBPF TC program looks up the destination in `cilium_srv6_policy`, prepends the SRv6 outer header (`H.Encaps`), and sends the packet into the underlay.

At **ingress**, the eBPF XDP program matches the destination SID against `cilium_srv6_sid`, strips the SRv6 header, and injects the inner packet into the correct VRF (`End.DT4` / `End.DT6`).

### BGP Control Plane

Cilium uses an integrated BGP control plane (backed by **GoBGP** or **FRRouting**) to:

- Advertise the node's SRv6 **locator prefix** to PE routers
- Exchange **VPNv4/VPNv6** routes with route targets for L3VPN
- Receive remote SIDs and program them into `cilium_srv6_policy`

No external router daemon required — Cilium manages BGP sessions directly via `CiliumBGPPeeringPolicy` CRDs.

### One BGP Session — All VRFs

!!! warning "Common misconception"
    Cilium does **not** open one BGP session per VRF, nor does it use BGP EVPN (L2VPN AFI 25). It behaves exactly like a traditional PE router: **one BGP session per peer**, carrying routes for all VRFs simultaneously over the **VPNv6 address family** (AFI 2 / SAFI 128).

A single `CiliumBGPPeeringPolicy` neighbor entry covers every tenant/VRF on that node:

```
Cilium Node (worker-1)  ←──── 1 TCP session (port 179) ────→  PE Router
                                         │
                         BGP UPDATE messages contain:
                         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │ AFI 2 / SAFI 128 (VPNv6)               │
                         │                                         │
                         │  RD 65100:100 | RT 65000:100           │
                         │    prefix: 10.0.1.0/24                  │
                         │    next-hop SRv6 SID: fc00:0:10::dt6:100│ ← VRF Tenant-A
                         │                                         │
                         │  RD 65100:200 | RT 65000:200           │
                         │    prefix: 10.0.2.0/24                  │
                         │    next-hop SRv6 SID: fc00:0:10::dt6:200│ ← VRF Tenant-B
                         │                                         │
                         │  RD 65100:300 | RT 65000:300           │
                         │    prefix: 10.0.3.0/24                  │
                         │    next-hop SRv6 SID: fc00:0:10::dt6:300│ ← VRF Tenant-C
                         └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The PE router uses the **Route Target (RT)** to import each prefix into the correct VRF — no separate BGP session needed.

### VPNv6 vs BGP EVPN — Key Differences

Both can carry L3 reachability for SRv6 tenants, but they are completely different address families:

| | **BGP VPNv6** (Cilium) | **BGP EVPN Type 5** |
|---|---|---|
| AFI / SAFI | 2 / 128 | 25 / 70 |
| NLRI type | VPNv6 prefix + RD | EVPN Route Type 5 (IP Prefix) |
| Original purpose | MPLS L3VPN (adapted for SRv6) | L2VPN, extended to L3 via Type 5 |
| Next-hop encoding | SRv6 SID as BGP next-hop | SRv6 SID in Tunnel Encap attribute |
| VRF signaling | Route Target extended community | Route Target extended community |
| MAC/L2 info | None — L3 only | Carries MAC+IP (Type 2) |
| Valid for SRv6 L3VPN? | Yes | Yes (RFC 9252 §5) |
| Cilium uses it? | Yes | No (implementation choice) |

!!! info "Both are valid for SRv6 L3VPN — but Cilium only speaks VPNv6"
    EVPN Type 5 (IP Prefix routes) over SRv6 is fully valid per RFC 9252 and widely deployed in carrier and DC fabrics. However, **Cilium's BGP control plane does not implement AFI 25 / SAFI 70 (L2VPN EVPN)**. It only negotiates VPNv6 (AFI 2 / SAFI 128). If your SRv6 fabric uses EVPN Type 5 for L3VPN, Cilium cannot peer directly with those PE routers.

### Interoperability Gap: Cilium ↔ EVPN Fabrics

This is a real-world limitation. If your network already runs EVPN Type 5 over SRv6 (common in DC fabrics using SONiC, Juniper, or Cisco NCS), you have three options:

| Option | How | Trade-off |
|--------|-----|-----------|
| **Route Reflector translation** | Deploy an RR (e.g. FRRouting) between Cilium and the PE. The RR peers with Cilium via VPNv6 and re-advertises towards the fabric via EVPN Type 5 | Extra hop in control plane; RR becomes a dependency |
| **Dual address-family on the PE** | Configure the PE to peer with Cilium using VPNv6 *and* continue using EVPN with the rest of the fabric | Requires PE support; routes must be redistributed between AFIs on the PE |
| **Wait for Cilium EVPN support** | EVPN is on the Cilium roadmap but not yet implemented for SRv6 | No ETA as of Cilium 1.15 |

```mermaid
graph LR
    C["Cilium Node\nVPNv6 only\nAFI 2/128"] -->|"VPNv6"| RR["Route Reflector\nFRRouting\n(bridge)"]
    RR -->|"EVPN Type 5\nAFI 25/70"| PE["PE Router\nEVPN fabric"]
    style RR fill:#1b5e2026,stroke:#1b5e20
```

## Installation

### Enable SRv6 via Helm

```bash
helm install cilium cilium/cilium \
  --namespace kube-system \
  --set bgpControlPlane.enabled=true \
  --set srv6.enabled=true \
  --set srv6.encapMode=srh        # or "reduced" for H.Encaps.Red
```

For Cilium 1.15+ with reduced encapsulation (recommended for production):

```yaml
# values.yaml
bgpControlPlane:
  enabled: true

srv6:
  enabled: true
  encapMode: reduced    # uses H.Encaps.Red — no SRH when single SID
```

```bash
helm upgrade cilium cilium/cilium -f values.yaml -n kube-system
```

## Configuration

### Step 1 — Assign a Locator to Each Node

Label each K8s node with its SRv6 locator prefix. Cilium allocates individual SIDs from this block for `End.DT4` / `End.DT6` behaviors.

```bash
kubectl label node worker-1 cilium.io/srv6-locator=fc00:0:10::/48
kubectl label node worker-2 cilium.io/srv6-locator=fc00:0:11::/48
```

### Step 2 — BGP Peering Policy

```yaml
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1
kind: CiliumBGPPeeringPolicy
metadata:
  name: srv6-peering
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    matchLabels:
      kubernetes.io/os: linux
  virtualRouters:
    - localASN: 65100
      exportPodCIDR: false          # pod CIDRs go via SRv6 L3VPN, not plain BGP
      neighbors:
        - peerAddress: "fc00:0:1::1/128"   # PE router SID/loopback
          peerASN: 65000
          families:
            - afi: ipv6
              safi: unicast
            - afi: ipv6
              safi: vpn-unicast     # VPNv6 for SRv6 L3VPN
      srv6:
        locatorPrefix: "fc00:0:10::/48"    # this node's SRv6 locator
```

### Step 3 — L3VPN (VRF) Mapping

```yaml
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1
kind: CiliumBGPAdvertisement
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-vpn
spec:
  advertisements:
    - advertisementType: "PodCIDR"
      service:
        addresses:
          - ClusterIP
      attributes:
        community:
          standard:
            - "65000:100"            # route target for Tenant A VRF
```

### Step 4 — Verify SRv6 State

```bash
# Check Cilium SRv6 is active
cilium status | grep -i srv6

# Inspect eBPF SRv6 maps
cilium bpf srv6 list

# Check BGP session state
cilium bgp peers

# Verify advertised/received SRv6 SIDs
cilium bgp routes advertised ipv6 vpn-unicast
cilium bgp routes received  ipv6 vpn-unicast
```

## Full Traffic Walk

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Pod as Pod A (10.0.1.5)
    participant eBPF as eBPF TC (egress)
    participant Fab as SRv6 Fabric
    participant eBPFr as eBPF XDP (ingress)
    participant PodB as Pod B (10.0.2.7)

    Pod->>eBPF: IPv4 packet → 10.0.2.7
    eBPF->>eBPF: lookup cilium_srv6_policy<br/>→ SID fc00:0:11::dt4
    eBPF->>Fab: SRv6 packet<br/>[fc00:0:11::dt4][IPv4: 10.0.2.7]
    Fab->>eBPFr: Deliver to worker-2<br/>DST = fc00:0:11::dt4
    eBPFr->>eBPFr: lookup cilium_srv6_sid<br/>→ VRF table 100
    eBPFr->>eBPFr: End.DT4: strip SRv6 header<br/>inject inner IPv4 into VRF 100
    eBPFr->>PodB: IPv4 packet → 10.0.2.7
```

## Comparison with Router-Based SRv6

| Aspect | Cilium (eBPF) | FRRouting | Cisco IOS-XR |
|--------|:-------------:|:---------:|:------------:|
| Data plane | eBPF (kernel bypass) | Linux kernel routing | ASIC / NPU |
| Control plane | GoBGP / FRR | FRR | IOS-XR BGP/IS-IS |
| L3VPN support | | | |
| Kubernetes-native | | | |
| CRD-driven config | | | |
| uSID support | Roadmap | | |
| Hardware offload | Roadmap | | |

## Observability

Cilium exports SRv6 telemetry via **Hubble** (Cilium's observability layer):

```bash
# Install Hubble CLI
hubble observe --type l3 --protocol SRv6

# Flow-level SRv6 visibility
hubble observe --namespace default \
  --output json | jq 'select(.destination.srv6_sid != null)'
```

Key Prometheus metrics exported:

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `cilium_srv6_encap_total` | Total SRv6 encapsulations by VRF |
| `cilium_srv6_decap_total` | Total SRv6 decapsulations by behavior |
| `cilium_srv6_drop_total` | SRv6 drops (no policy match, invalid SID) |
| `cilium_bgp_session_state` | BGP session state per peer |

# zebra-rs: Rust Routing Stack with an eBPF SRv6 Data Plane

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/zebra-rs/
Path: implementations/zebra-rs.md
Summary: SRv6 with zebra-rs and its cradle-rs eBPF data plane — a Rust routing stack (IS-IS, OSPFv3, BGP) whose learned routes program an XDP/TC data plane implementing the full RFC 8986 behavior set plus RFC 9800 uSID and REPLACE-C-SID compression.

# SRv6 with zebra-rs (eBPF)

**zebra-rs** is a BGP, OSPF, and IS-IS routing stack written from scratch in Rust, with SRv6, SR-MPLS, L3VPN, and EVPN extensions. Its eBPF data plane is **cradle-rs** — an XDP/TC forwarding engine built on [aya](https://aya-rs.dev) (pure Rust, no clang/libbpf) that zebra-rs launches and programs directly from its routing state.

The combination is an open-source SRv6 router: every route the protocols compute — IS-IS SRv6 locators, BGP L3VPN service SIDs, EVPN MAC routes — is installed into eBPF maps *in addition to* the Linux kernel FIB. Several SRv6 behaviors that the mainline kernel cannot forward at all (EVPN L2 decap, REPLACE-C-SID, egress protection, P2MP replication) run only on the eBPF path.

!!! info "Versions"
    Facts on this page reflect **zebra-rs 26.7.7** with the bundled **cradle-rs 0.9.8** engine, BDD-tested on **Linux 6.8**. Both projects are AGPL-licensed: [zebra-rs](https://github.com/zebra-rs/zebra-rs) · [cradle-rs](https://github.com/zebra-rs/cradle-rs).

## Why zebra-rs + cradle-rs?

Cilium brought SRv6 to eBPF for Kubernetes, but its BGP control plane only *advertises* routes — it never installs learned routes into the data path. zebra-rs approaches it from the routing side: a full multi-protocol routing stack (IS-IS, OSPFv3, BGP with VPNv4/VPNv6/EVPN/SR Policy address families) is the source of truth, and the eBPF engine is simply its FIB.

What makes it distinctive:

- **Learned routes program eBPF.** IS-IS SRv6 locators, BGP L3VPN (VPNv4/VPNv6 with SRv6 SIDs), and BGP EVPN over SRv6 all land in the eBPF FIB through a gRPC tee — the direction Cilium's BGP control plane doesn't support.
- **The widest open-source behavior set.** The full RFC 8986 catalog including End.T, End.DX2/DX2V, End.DT2U/DT2M, End.B6.Encaps, plus **both** RFC 9800 compression flavors (NEXT-C-SID *and* REPLACE-C-SID), the PSP/USP/USD flavors, End.M egress protection, and RFC 9524 End.Replicate.
- **A reverse channel.** The data plane's MAC learning streams back up (`WatchFdb`), driving EVPN Type-2 origination and withdrawal — the eBPF data plane is a control-plane *participant*, not just a sink.
- **Rust end to end.** Control plane, user-space loader, and the eBPF programs themselves are Rust (aya); no clang or libbpf in the build.

## Supported SRv6 Behaviors

All rows marked supported are BDD-proven in the projects' test suites (feature names like `cradle_srv6`, `cradle_srv6_usid`, `isis_srv6_base`, `l3vpn_bgp_v6` run the actual daemons in network namespaces and assert forwarding).

### Headend

| Behavior | Notes | Status |
|----------|-------|:------:|
| `H.Encaps` | Multi-SID SRH imposition (TC stage) | |
| `H.Encaps.Red` | The default — single SID means no SRH on the wire | |
| `H.Encaps.L2` / `L2.Red` | MAC-in-SRv6 (next-header 143) for EVPN | |
| `H.Insert` | TI-LFA repair imposition (IPv6) | |

### Endpoint

| Behavior | Notes | Status |
|----------|-------|:------:|
| `End`, `End.X`, `End.T` | SRH walk, adjacency cross-connect, table-scoped lookup | |
| `End.DT4` / `DT6` / `DT46` | Per-VRF decap; End.DT46 is the BGP L3VPN service SID | |
| `End.DX4` / `DX6` | Decap + cross-connect to the CE adjacency | |
| `End.DX2` / `DX2V` | EVPN VPWS E-Line; DX2V demuxes the inner 802.1Q VID | |
| `End.DT2U` / `DT2M` | EVPN unicast bridge / BUM flood (eBPF only) | |
| `End.B6.Encaps` / `.Red` | Binding SID: End walk + policy push | |
| `End.M` | Mirror SID egress protection (draft-ietf-rtgwg-srv6-egress-protection) | |
| `End.Replicate` | RFC 9524 SR P2MP replication segment | |
| `End.BM`, `End.S`, `End.AN/AS/AD/AM` | Service programming out of scope | |

### Compression (RFC 9800) and Flavors

| Feature | Notes | Status |
|---------|-------|:------:|
| **NEXT-C-SID (uSID)**: `uN`, `uA`, `uA (LIB)`, `uT`, `uDT4/6/46`, `uDX4/6` | 16-bit micro-SIDs, blocks 16/32/48 | |
| **REPLACE-C-SID**: `End`, `End.X` | 32/16-bit C-SIDs — container walk + DA index argument. **eBPF only** — Linux 6.8 has no REPLACE seg6local op | |
| **PSP / USP / USD** | RFC 8986 §4.16 flavors on End / End.X / uN / uA | |
| `uB6` | | |

## Architecture

### One Routing Stack, Two FIBs

zebra-rs runs as a single tokio-based process; each protocol is an async task feeding a central RIB. Turning on the eBPF data plane is two config knobs:

```
system {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}
interface enp0s6 {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}
```

`system ebpf enabled true` makes zebra-rs spawn and supervise the `cradle` engine as a managed child process (crash → respawn with backoff, full FIB state **replayed** into the fresh instance) and tees every route install to it over gRPC (`cradle.v1`, default endpoint `unix:cradle/grpc`). `interface  ebpf enabled true` attaches the XDP + TC programs to that interface; the port follows the interface's VRF binding.

### XDP for Decap, TC for Encap

cradle-rs compiles one fully-inlined eBPF program per hook and splits SRv6 across them deliberately:

| Stage | SRv6 work | Why there |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| **XDP** (`cradle_xdp`) | All endpoint behaviors: `End` SRH walk, `uN` shift-and-forward, `End.DT*`/`DX*` decap, `End.DT2U/DT2M` L2 decap, `End.M`, `End.B6` policy push — plus MAC-in-SRv6 L2 encap | Native XDP re-runs `eth_type_trans` after the header adjustment, so the decapsulated inner packet enters TC with a correct `skb->protocol` |
| **TC** (`cradle_tc`) | `H.Encaps` / `H.Encaps.Red` / `H.Insert` imposition, FIB forwarding, and the `End.Replicate` clone (`bpf_clone_redirect` is TC-only) | Encap egress needs an explicit L2 rewrite — `bpf_redirect_neigh` would build the L2 header from the stale inner `skb->protocol` |

A metadata channel (`CradleXdpMeta`) carries the VRF or bridge-domain from an XDP decap to the TC forwarding lookup, guarded by a per-instance random cookie so stale metadata can't cross a veth hop into a neighbor's TC stage.

### SRv6 eBPF Maps

| eBPF Map | Key | Value | Purpose |
|----------|-----|-------|---------|
| `SRV6_LOCALSID` | SID (LPM trie) | behavior, flavors, VRF, nexthop, SID structure | Local SID table, probed before the IPv6 FIB |
| `SRV6_ENCAP` | Nexthop ID | Segment list (≤6 SIDs) + encap mode | Per-nexthop `H.Encaps` / `H.Insert` state |
| `SRV6_ENCAP_SRC` | — | IPv6 address | Outer source address for imposition |
| `FIB4_VRF` / `FIB6_VRF` | VRF + prefix (LPM) | FIB entry | Inner lookup for `End.DT4/DT6/DT46` |
| `FDB` | MAC + VLAN | port or remote `End.DT2U` SID | EVPN L2: remote entries carry the peer's SID |
| `XCONNECT` / `XCONNECT_VLAN` | AC ifindex / (table, VID) | Remote `End.DX2`/`DX2V` SID | VPWS E-Line ingress |
| `REPL_SEG` / `REPL_SID` | SID / ifindex | Branch list / per-copy target | RFC 9524 replication tree, EVPN BUM slots |
| `MIRROR` | Context + prefix (LPM) | behavior, VRF | `End.M` egress-protection mirror contexts |

## Control Plane

| Producer | What it programs | Reference |
|----------|------------------|-----------|
| **IS-IS** | SRv6 Locator TLV 27 (with Algorithm for Flex-Algo), End/uN node SIDs, End.X/uA adjacency SIDs, End.T/uT for VRF-bound locators, SID Structure sub-sub-TLV | RFC 9352, RFC 9350 |
| **OSPFv3** | SRv6-Locator-LSA (`0xA02A`), End/uN + SID Structure, per-adjacency End.X/uA in the E-Router-LSA | RFC 9513 |
| **BGP L3VPN** | VPNv4/VPNv6 with a per-VRF `End.DT46` SID in the Prefix-SID attribute (SRv6 L3 Service TLV); VPN-IPv4 over an IPv6 next-hop | RFC 9252, RFC 8669, RFC 8950 |
| **BGP EVPN** | Type-2 → `End.DT2U`, Type-3 → `End.DT2M` + BUM replication slots, Type-5 → per-VRF `End.DT46`, VPWS Type-1 → `End.DX2`; MAC mobility sequencing fed by the `WatchFdb` learn/age stream | RFC 9252, RFC 8214, RFC 9136 |
| **BGP SR Policy** | Binding SID (SAFI 73) → `End.B6.Encaps`, color-based steering to a BSID | RFC 9256, RFC 9830 |
| **TI-LFA** | Repair segment lists as `H.Insert`/`H.Encaps` backups, per-Flex-Algo TI-LFA, PSP on the repair carrier | RFC 9855 |
| **Egress protection** | Mirror SID (`End.M`) advertised in IS-IS; live L3VPN failover on egress PE death | draft-ietf-rtgwg-srv6-egress-protection |

One deliberate design detail: the per-VRF BGP service-SID functions are allocated from a band (`0x0040`–`0xDFFF`) kept below the IS-IS End.X/uA range (`0xE000+`), following the IOS-XR uSID GIB/LIB convention — so BGP and IS-IS share a single locator without collisions.

!!! note "eBPF-only behaviors"
    zebra-rs installs the classic behaviors (`End`, `End.X`, `uN`, `uA`, `End.T`, `End.DT4/6/46`, `End.DX4/6`, `End.B6.Encaps`, `H.Encaps`) into the kernel as `seg6`/`seg6local` routes *and* the eBPF engine. But `End.DT2U`/`DT2M` (EVPN L2), `End.DX2`/`DX2V` (VPWS), `End.M`, `End.Replicate`, `uT`, and the REPLACE-C-SID behaviors have **no mainline-kernel equivalent** — for those, cradle-rs is the only data plane. EVPN over SRv6 on Linux effectively requires it.

## Installation

Prebuilt `.deb` packages exist for Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 / 26.04 (x86_64 and ARM64):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://zebra.rs/install.sh | bash
```

The `cradle-rs` engine ships as a separate Debian package that zebra-rs recommends and pulls in automatically; zebra-rs finds it at `/usr/bin/cradle` with no further setup. Building cradle-rs from source needs a nightly Rust toolchain with `rust-src` and `bpf-linker` — no clang or libbpf.

## Configuration

Configuration is YANG-modeled with a candidate/running commit model, and the same tree can be expressed as Cisco-style CLI, YAML, JSON, or `set` commands (`vtyctl apply -f zebra.yaml`). The snippets below come from the project's book and BDD suite — they are validated, running configurations.

### Step 1 — Define an SRv6 Locator

```
segment-routing {
  locator LOC1 {
    prefix fcbb:bbbb:1::/48;
    behavior usid;
  }
}
```

`behavior usid` selects RFC 9800 NEXT-C-SID (micro-SID) format; `behavior replace` selects REPLACE-C-SID; omitting it gives classic full-length RFC 8986 SIDs. Optional per-locator `flavor {psp|usp|usd}` and `vrf ` (which turns the node SID into `End.T`/`uT`) are supported.

### Step 2 — Advertise it in the IGP

```
router {
  isis {
    net 49.0000.0000.0000.0001.00;
    is-type level-2-only;
    segment-routing {
      srv6 {
        locator LOC1;
      }
    }
    interface enp0s6 {
      circuit-type level-2-only;
      ipv6 {
        enabled true;
      }
      network-type point-to-point;
    }
  }
}
```

(OSPFv3 is analogous: `router ospfv3  } }`. OSPFv2 cannot carry SRv6 — it is IPv6-only on the wire.)

### Step 3 — BGP L3VPN over SRv6

```
router bgp {
  global {
    as 65000;
  }
  segment-routing {
    srv6 {
      locator LOC1;
    }
  }
  vrf vrf1 {
    rd 65000:1;
    encapsulation srv6;
    neighbor 10.100.0.2 {
      remote-as 65001;
    }
    afi-safi ipv4 {
      network 192.168.5.0/24;
    }
    afi-safi ipv6 {
      network 2001:db8:5::/64;
    }
  }
}

vrf vrf1 {
  ipv4 {
    route-target {
      import 65000:1;
      export 65000:1;
    }
  }
  ipv6 {
    route-target {
      import 65000:1;
      export 65000:1;
    }
  }
}
```

`encapsulation srv6` switches the VRF from MPLS labels to a per-VRF `End.DT46` SID — one SID serves both VPNv4 and VPNv6. EVPN L2 uses the same pattern (`afi-safi evpn` + `encapsulation srv6`) to advertise `End.DT2U`/`End.DT2M` SIDs.

### Step 4 — Enable the eBPF Data Plane

```
system {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}
interface enp0s6 {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}
```

### Step 5 — Verify

```
zebra> show ebpf
eBPF data plane
  System ebpf:     enabled
  FIB tee:         enabled
  Engine:          managed (pid 168157), up 42s
  Engine restarts: 1
  ...

zebra> show ebpf srv6        # SRv6 local SIDs and transit encaps
zebra> show ebpf ipv6 vrf vrf1
zebra> show ebpf stats       # datapath counters, per-behavior
```

Every `show ebpf` command takes a trailing `json` for machine-readable output.

## Full Traffic Walk

An L3VPN packet through a uSID fabric — ingress imposition in TC, everything else in XDP:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CE1 as CE A
    participant PE1 as PE1 cradle_tc<br/>(H.Encaps.Red)
    participant P as P router cradle_xdp<br/>(uN)
    participant PE2 as PE2 cradle_xdp<br/>(End.DT46)
    participant CE2 as CE B

    CE1->>PE1: IPv4 packet (VRF vrf1)
    PE1->>PE1: FIB4_VRF hit → nexthop with SRv6 segs<br/>SRV6_ENCAP: outer DA fcbb:bbbb:3:2::/…
    PE1->>P: [IPv6 DA=uSID carrier][IPv4] (no SRH)
    P->>P: SRV6_LOCALSID LPM hit (uN)<br/>shift-and-forward: consume own uSID
    P->>PE2: [IPv6 DA advanced][IPv4]
    PE2->>PE2: SRV6_LOCALSID hit (End.DT46)<br/>XDP decap → VRF metadata → TC lookup in FIB4_VRF
    PE2->>CE2: IPv4 packet (VRF vrf1)
```

## Comparison with Other Open-Source SRv6 Implementations

| Aspect | zebra-rs + cradle-rs | Cilium | FRRouting + kernel |
|--------|:--------------------:|:------:|:------------------:|
| Data plane | eBPF XDP + TC (aya, Rust) | eBPF | Linux kernel seg6 |
| Control plane | Integrated IS-IS / OSPFv3 / BGP | GoBGP-based (advertise-only) | FRR daemons |
| Learned routes → eBPF | | | n/a (kernel) |
| L3VPN over SRv6 | End.DT46 | End.DT4/DT6 | |
| EVPN L2 over SRv6 | DT2U/DT2M/DX2 | | (no kernel behavior) |
| uSID (NEXT-C-SID) | | Roadmap | |
| REPLACE-C-SID | | | |
| TI-LFA / Flex-Algo | | | Partial |
| Kubernetes CNI | (kube-proxy replacement, Cilium-API compatible) | | |

Performance context: cradle-rs's DIR-24-8 FIB engine sustains **~51 ns lookups at 1M routes** (measured via `BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN` on the full TC program); SRv6 forwarding itself is validated functionally by the BDD suites rather than benchmarked separately.

## Observability & AI Integration

- **`show ebpf stats`** exposes per-behavior datapath counters (SRv6 encap/decap, End, uSID shift, PSP/USP/USD, REPLACE, B6, End.M, replicate, drops), also as JSON.
- **Hubble compatibility**: cradle-rs serves the Hubble Observer/Peer gRPC API from an eBPF flow ringbuf — the stock `hubble` CLI, `hubble-relay`, and `hubble-ui` work against a cradle node.
- **MCP server**: zebra-rs is the first routing daemon to ship a native [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. AI agents inspect the same RIB, BGP, and IS-IS state an operator sees:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "zebra-rs": { "command": "vtyctl", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

## Further Reading

- [uSID Compression](https://srv6.md/topics/usid-compression/) -- NEXT-C-SID and REPLACE-C-SID, both of which this stack implements
- [Network Programming](https://srv6.md/topics/network-programming/) -- The RFC 8986 behavior catalog
- [TI-LFA](https://srv6.md/topics/ti-lfa/) -- Fast reroute, implemented here over SRv6 with PSP repair
- [Cilium (eBPF)](https://srv6.md/implementations/cilium/) -- The other eBPF SRv6 implementation, from the Kubernetes side
- [Linux Kernel](https://srv6.md/implementations/linux-kernel/) -- The seg6 data plane zebra-rs programs in parallel

## References

1. [zebra-rs on GitHub](https://github.com/zebra-rs/zebra-rs) -- The routing stack: BGP, OSPF, IS-IS with SRv6/SR-MPLS/L3VPN/EVPN
2. [cradle-rs on GitHub](https://github.com/zebra-rs/cradle-rs) -- The eBPF L2–L7 data plane and Kubernetes CNI
3. [zebra.rs documentation](https://zebra.rs/docs.html) -- Install, configuration model, and per-protocol guides
4. [RFC 9252 - BGP Overlay Services Based on SRv6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9252) -- L3VPN and EVPN service SID signaling implemented by zebra-rs
5. [RFC 9800 - SRv6 Segment List Compression](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9800) -- NEXT-C-SID and REPLACE-C-SID, both supported in the eBPF data plane
6. [RFC 9524 - SR Replication Segments for P2MP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9524) -- End.Replicate, used for EVPN BUM over SRv6 P2MP

# Vinbero: Go and eBPF SRv6 Data Plane

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/vinbero/
Path: implementations/vinbero.md
Summary: SRv6 with Vinbero — a Go daemon whose eBPF data plane implements the RFC 8986 behaviors, EVPN L2VPN with multi-homing, the RFC 9433 mobile user plane, and service programming proxies, driven by an in-process GoBGP speaker.

# SRv6 with Vinbero (eBPF/Go)

**Vinbero** is an SRv6 implementation in two Go binaries: `vinberod`, a daemon that owns an eBPF data plane and an in-process BGP speaker, and `vinbero`, a CLI that drives it over Connect RPC.
Forwarding happens in eBPF; the control plane exists to populate its maps.

Its coverage runs in two directions the other open-source stacks rarely take: the **mobile user plane** (RFC 9433 GTP-U ⇄ SRv6, signalled by BGP MUP) and **service programming** proxies that put SR-unaware appliances inside an SRv6 chain.
Two gaps come with that.
There is no IGP, so the underlay is plain IPv6 routing and BGP carries every service.
RFC 9800 SID compression is on the roadmap and not implemented.

!!! info "Versions"
    Facts on this page reflect **Vinbero 0.1.1**, Apache-2.0 licensed: [takehaya/vinbero](https://github.com/takehaya/vinbero).
    The eBPF objects are load-tested in CI on kernels 6.1, 6.6, 6.12, and 7.0; the documented floor is Linux 5.15.

## Supported SRv6 Behaviors

Many of these behaviors have a runnable scenario under [`examples/`](https://github.com/takehaya/vinbero/tree/main/examples), built from network namespaces with setup, test, and teardown scripts, and the BGP services are verified against FRRouting in CI with containerlab.

| Group | Behaviors | Status |
|-------|-----------|:------:|
| Headend | `H.Encaps`, `H.Encaps.L2`, `H.Insert` (all `.Red`) | |
| Endpoint | `End`, `End.X`, `End.T`, `End.DT4/6/46`, `End.DX4/6` | |
| Endpoint (L2) | `End.DX2`, `End.DX2V`, `End.DT2U`, `End.DT2M` | |
| Binding SID | `End.B6.Encaps`, `End.B6.Insert` (both `.Red`) | |
| Mobile user plane (RFC 9433) | `H.M.GTP4.D`, `H.M.GTP6.D`, `End.M.GTP6.D`/`.D.Di`, `End.M.GTP4.E`, `End.M.GTP6.E`, `Args.Mob.Session` | |
| Service programming | `End.AS` (static), `End.AD` (dynamic), `End.AM` (masquerading), `End.AN` (SR-aware) | |
| Flavors | PSP / USP / USD | |
| Compression (RFC 9800) | NEXT-C-SID (uSID), REPLACE-C-SID, `End.LBS`/`XLBS` | |
| Other | `End.BM`, `End.NSH`, `End.Replicate`, `End.MAP`, `End.Limit` | |

## Architecture

One XDP program per interface dispatches behaviors through `PROG_ARRAY` tail calls, one slot per behavior.
Reserved slots take operator-supplied XDP plugins registered at runtime, each configured per SID from JSON marshalled through the plugin's own BTF.
A separate and much smaller TC program handles BUM replication, because `bpf_clone_redirect` exists only in TC.

Packets enter through an ingress front door that maps `{ifindex, vlan}` to a VRF, then take one of three paths: an LPM lookup in the local SID table, which yields a behavior and its per-SID parameters; an LPM lookup in the headend tables, which encapsulates towards a service SID after resolving an SR Policy if the route carries a color; or the L2 tables.
A headend entry can point at a group of up to eight weighted paths, chosen by a hash of the inner flow and masked by a liveness bitmap that a userspace prober updates for fast reroute.
That same hash goes into the outer flow label (RFC 6437), because every encapsulated packet between one pair of PEs otherwise shares an outer source and destination, which pins a whole site-to-site tunnel to one transit ECMP path.

One deliberate split: Vinbero holds **no per-VRF IP routing table in eBPF**.
`End.DT4/DT6/DT46` decapsulate and hand the inner packet to the kernel VRF device the SID names, and the kernel FIB does the lookup.
eBPF owns what the kernel cannot do: the SRv6 service tables, the L2 tables, and the GTP behaviors.

## Control Plane

GoBGP v4 runs as a library inside `vinberod` (`--bgp-enabled`), so a received route becomes an eBPF map write inside a single process, with no sidecar.
Each entry carries an owner tag, so a withdrawal removes what that route installed and leaves an operator's static entries in place.

| Address family | What it programs | Reference |
|----------------|------------------|-----------|
| VPNv4 / VPNv6 | RD/RT demux, SRv6 Service TLV (incl. §4 SID-structure transposition) to `H.Encaps` towards the remote `End.DT4`/`DT6` | RFC 9252 |
| EVPN (L2VPN) | RT2 remote MACs, RT3 BUM peers (`End.DT2M`), RT4 Ethernet Segment with RFC 8584 DF election and Local-Bias split horizon, RT1 aliasing | RFC 9252, RFC 7432, RFC 8584 |
| SR Policy (SAFI 73) | `{color, endpoint}` to a transport SID list, weighted segment lists, color steering in the data plane | RFC 9256 |
| BGP MUP (SAFI 85) | ISD/DSD segment discovery and T1ST/T2ST sessions to GTP downlink `H.Encaps` and uplink F-TEID entries | `draft-mpmz-bess-mup-safi` |
| IPv6 unicast | Injected into the kernel FIB | RFC 4760 |

Route targets bind per family and per direction in one command, `vinbero vrf-bgp bind --vrf vrf100 --rt vpnv4:65100:100:both`, which drives both import filtering and auto-advertise: connected and static prefixes, EVPN RT2/RT3/RT4 from the bridge lifecycle, local SR Policies, and local MUP routes.

## Installation

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/takehaya/vinbero/main/scripts/install_vinbero.sh | sudo bash
sudo vinberod -c vinbero.yml   # --bgp-enabled to start the BGP speaker
```

## Configuration

`vinbero.yml` declares only what must exist at boot: which interfaces get XDP (`internal.devices`), the attach mode (`internal.bpf.device_mode`, either `driver` or `generic` for veth labs), the RPC bind address, and optional map pinning that carries data-plane state across a restart.
Everything else is created at runtime.

```bash
# L3VPN: a VRF is one object (kernel device + vrf_id + ingress membership)
vinbero vrf create --name vrf100 --table-id 100 --members eth2 --enable-l3mdev-rule
vinbero sid create --trigger-prefix fc00:3::3/128 --action END_DT4 --vrf-name vrf100

# EVPN: a bridge domain behind an L2 VRF facet
vinbero vrf bridge-attach --vrf evi-100 --name br100 --bd-id 100 --members eth1
vinbero sid create --trigger-prefix fc00:2::2/128 --action END_DT2 --bd-id 100 --bridge-name br100

# Static headend (BGP writes the equivalent entries once a session is up)
vinbero hv4 create --trigger-prefix 10.2.0.0/24 --src-addr fc00:1::1 \
    --segments fc00:2::2,fc00:3::3

vinbero sid list && vinbero stats show
```

A VRF cannot be deleted while a SID, an ingress access circuit, or a BGP binding still references it: the daemon refuses and names the reference.

- [zebra-rs (eBPF)](https://srv6.md/implementations/zebra-rs/) -- The other eBPF stack, approached from the routing side
- [Cilium (eBPF)](https://srv6.md/implementations/cilium/) -- eBPF SRv6 from the Kubernetes side
- [Linux Kernel](https://srv6.md/implementations/linux-kernel/) -- The seg6 data plane Vinbero bypasses, and the VRF FIB it still relies on

## References

2. [Vinbero roadmap](https://github.com/takehaya/vinbero/blob/main/docs/loadmap.md) -- Per-behavior support status

# SRv6 on Cisco IOS-XR: uSID and L3VPN Configuration

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/cisco-ios-xr/
Path: implementations/cisco-ios-xr.md
Summary: Configure SRv6 on Cisco IOS-XR: supported NCS, ASR 9000 and Cisco 8000 platforms, uSID locator and IS-IS setup, L3VPN over SRv6, and verification commands.

# SRv6 on Cisco IOS-XR

Cisco IOS-XR provides comprehensive SRv6 support across NCS and ASR platforms.

## Supported Platforms

- NCS 5500 / 5700 Series
- NCS 540 Series
- ASR 9000 Series
- Cisco 8000 Series (Silicon One)

## Basic Configuration

```cisco
!! Enable SRv6
segment-routing
 srv6
  locators
   locator MAIN
    micro-segment behavior unode psp-usd
    prefix fc00:0:1::/48
   !
  !
 !
!

!! Enable SRv6 in IS-IS
router isis CORE
 address-family ipv6 unicast
  segment-routing srv6
   locator MAIN
  !
 !
!

!! SRv6-based L3VPN
vrf CUSTOMER-A
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  import route-target 100:1
  export route-target 100:1
 !
!

router bgp 65000
 vrf CUSTOMER-A
  address-family ipv4 unicast
   segment-routing srv6
    locator MAIN
    alloc mode per-vrf
   !
  !
 !
!
```

## Verification Commands

```cisco
show segment-routing srv6 locator
show segment-routing srv6 sid
show segment-routing srv6 manager
show isis segment-routing srv6 locators
show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf CUSTOMER-A
```

# SRv6 on Cisco IOS-XE: uSID Configuration Guide

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/cisco-ios-xe/
Path: implementations/cisco-ios-xe.md
Summary: Configure SRv6 uSID on Cisco IOS-XE 8000 Series Secure Routers: F3216 locators, IS-IS, per-VRF L3VPN SIDs, Flex-Algo, TI-LFA and verification commands.

# SRv6 on Cisco IOS-XE

SRv6 on Cisco has long been an [IOS-XR](https://srv6.md/implementations/cisco-ios-xr/) story (NCS, ASR 9000, Cisco 8000). That changed with **IOS-XE 26.1**: Cisco's enterprise/edge operating system now ships validated SRv6 uSID support, documented in the 2026 CVD [*Quantum-Safe SRv6 Fabric for Mission-Critical Networks*](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/solutions/CVD/Campus/SRv6_Fabric-Mission-Critical_Networks.html). This brings SRv6 to the WAN-edge and branch platforms that historically terminated SD-WAN or DMVPN.

## Supported Platforms (validated in the CVD)

- Cisco 8000 Series Secure Routers (G2): 8161-G2 (compact edge), 8375-E-G2 / 8475-G2 (branch/campus edge), 8550-G2 / 8570-G2 (aggregation hubs)
- Catalyst 8000 edge family (SR-TE/ePBR feature lineage)

## Feature Highlights

| Feature | IOS-XE support |
|---------|----------------|
| uSID format | **F3216 only** (`format usid-f3216`) — 32-bit block, 16-bit node, 16-bit function |
| Headend encapsulation | `H.Encaps.Red` (reduced) |
| End behaviors | `uN`, `uA`, `uDT4`, `uDT6`, `uDT46`, `End.DTMC4` (multicast VRF decap) |
| L3VPN SID allocation | **`alloc-mode per-vrf` only** — per-prefix allocation is not supported |
| IGP | IS-IS with multi-topology IPv6, wide metrics |
| SR-TE | Per-Destination and Per-Flow policies, ODN/Automated Steering, ePBR + NBAR classification |
| Flex-Algo | Yes, with per-algorithm locators |
| TI-LFA | Yes, with node-protecting / SRLG-disjoint / linecard-disjoint tiebreakers |
| Performance measurement | Two-way active probes, delay advertisement into IS-IS, liveness detection |
| Multicast | BGP MVPN with SRv6 ingress replication (`srv6-mcast ingress-replication partitioned`) |

## Basic Configuration

```cisco
! SRv6 process: encapsulation source + F3216 locator
segment-routing srv6
 encapsulation
  source-address FC00::1
  traffic-class propagate
 locators
  locator MAIN
   prefix FCBB:DEAD:1::/48
   format usid-f3216

! IS-IS underlay — multi-topology IPv6 + locator advertisement
router isis 1
 net 49.0000.fc00.0001.00
 is-type level-2-only
 metric-style wide
 advertise link attributes
 distribute link-state
 !
 address-family ipv6
  multi-topology
  router-id Loopback0
  segment-routing srv6
   locator MAIN
   level-2
  fast-reroute ti-lfa level-2

! L3VPN over SRv6 (per-VRF Service SID)
router bgp 65001
 segment-routing srv6
  locator MAIN
 !
 address-family vpnv4
  segment-routing srv6
   locator MAIN
   alloc-mode per-vrf
  neighbor FC00::3 activate
  neighbor FC00::3 send-community extended
```

!!! warning "Ethernet interfaces must be point-to-point"
    IOS-XE treats Ethernet as broadcast by default, which creates IS-IS pseudonodes that **silently break** adjacency-SID allocation and SR-TE path computation. `isis network point-to-point` on every SRv6 core interface is non-negotiable.

!!! note "Per-VRF allocation only"
    Unlike IOS-XR, IOS-XE supports only `alloc-mode per-vrf` for L3VPN Service SIDs — one `uDT4`/`uDT6` per VRF, with the egress doing a full VRF lookup after decapsulation. Per-prefix mode does not exist.

## Verification Commands

```cisco
show segment-routing srv6 locator
show segment-routing srv6 sid
show isis srv6 locators
show segment-routing traffic-eng policy name * detail
show performance-measurement summary
show isis ipv6 fast-reroute summary
show ip bgp vpnv4 all
```

## Further Reading

- [Mission-Critical Networks](https://srv6.md/use-cases/mission-critical/) - The validated design that debuted SRv6 on IOS-XE
- [Cisco IOS-XR](https://srv6.md/implementations/cisco-ios-xr/) - Cisco's service-provider SRv6 implementation
- [uSID / SRv6 Compression](https://srv6.md/topics/usid-compression/) - The F3216 format explained

## References

1. [Cisco CVD: Quantum-Safe SRv6 Fabric for Mission-Critical Networks](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/solutions/CVD/Campus/SRv6_Fabric-Mission-Critical_Networks.html) - Validated design and configuration baseline for SRv6 on IOS-XE 26.1
2. [Cisco 8000 Series Secure Routers](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/products/networking/wan/routers/8000-series-secure-routers/index.html) - Platform family validated for SRv6 uSID on IOS-XE

# Juniper SRv6 on Junos: uSID, L3VPN, Flex-Algo and TI-LFA Guide

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/juniper/
Path: implementations/juniper.md
Summary: Configure SRv6 on Juniper Junos and Junos Evolved: platforms and releases, uSID locators, IS-IS, L3VPN and Internet over SRv6, Flex-Algo, TI-LFA and verification.

# SRv6 on Juniper Junos

Juniper implements SRv6 in **Junos OS** (MX Series) and **Junos OS Evolved** (PTX and ACX7000 Series), with both full-length (classic) SIDs and micro-SIDs (uSID, the RFC 9800 NEXT-CSID flavor). This guide walks through a complete uSID deployment — locator, IS-IS, L3VPN and Internet services, Flex-Algo and TI-LFA — following the structure of Juniper's validated design for SRv6 core and edge, and shows the commands to verify each step.

!!! info "Juniper Validated Design"
    The [JVD for Service Provider SRv6 Core and Edge](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/jvd/jvd-sp-core-edge-srv6-01-01/service_provider_srv6_core_and_edge_-_phase_1_juniper_validated_design_jvd.html) was qualified on Junos 24.4R2 and Junos Evolved 24.4R2 with MX480 (MPC7E, MPC10E), MX10004 (LC9600), MX2010 (MPC11E), MX304 and PTX10002-36QDD. It uses uSID only (F3216 format, blocks from `5f00::/16`), Flex-Algo 0/128/129, TI-LFA with microloop avoidance, uDT46 L3VPN and uDX2 EVPN-VPWS.

## Platforms and Releases

| Capability | Junos OS (MX) | Junos OS Evolved |
|------------|---------------|------------------|
| SRv6 in IS-IS, classic SIDs | 20.3R1 (MX240/480/960/2000; MPC7E/8E/9E or newer) | PTX10002-36QDD 24.2R2, PTX10008 24.4R1-S2 |
| L3 services over SRv6 (BGP) | 20.4R1 (MX and vMX); MX304 22.2R3; MX10004 22.3R1 | PTX10002-36QDD 24.2R2; PTX10008 24.4R1-S2 |
| uSID in IS-IS transport | 23.4R1 (MX204 through MX10016) | PTX10008 24.4R1-S2 |
| uSID with L3VPN and IS-IS on ACX | — | ACX7024/7100/7509 23.2R1; ACX7024X/7332/7348 23.4R1 |
| uSID with TI-LFA, microloop avoidance, Flex-Algo | 23.4R1 | ACX7024X/7348 24.2R1 |
| SRv6 Flex-Algo | Classic SIDs by 21.2R1 (inter-level leaking); uSID 23.4R1 | ACX7024/7100/7509 23.1R1 |
| SRv6 microloop avoidance (IS-IS) | 21.1R1 | PTX10002-36QDD 24.4R1 |

Release numbers are the "introduced" values from [Juniper Feature Explorer](https://apps.juniper.net/feature-explorer/); check it for your exact platform and line card. **cRPD** supports SRv6 in IS-IS and L3 services in BGP with limitations (no flavor or Flex-Algo options on End SIDs, no ARM64). There is no official SRv6 support statement for vJunos-router.

## Building Blocks

| Junos object | Hierarchy | What it is |
|--------------|-----------|------------|
| **Block** | `routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block` | The uSID block (default 32 bits, the only length on ACX), with global (GIB) and local (LIB) ID ranges |
| **Locator** | `routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator` | The node's /48 (with `micro-sid`) or classic locator; can be bound to a Flex-Algo |
| **uN / End SID** | `protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator  micro-node-sid` | Advertised by IS-IS; without it the local locator is not even installed |
| **uA / End.X SID** | `protocols isis interface  level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment` | Per-adjacency SID, `protected` or `unprotected` |
| **Service SID** | `routing-instances  protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator ` | uDT4/uDT6/uDT46 (or End.DT4/6/46) per VRF |

The default uSID length is 16 bits. In each block the GIB defaults to `0x0000–0xDFFF` (static) and the LIB to `0xE000–0xFFFF` (dynamic). With no flavor configured, `micro-sid` SIDs use **PSP and USD**.

## Step 1: Platform Prerequisites (MX)

```junos
set chassis network-services enhanced-ip
set routing-options resolution preserve-nexthop-hierarchy
set routing-options forwarding-table srv6-chain-merge
```

`enhanced-ip` is needed on MX only. The other two enable the chained, hierarchical next-hop structures that SRv6 services resolve through; the JVD sets them on every router.

## Step 2: uSID Block and Locator

The example uses the IANA SRv6 SID block `5f00::/16` ([RFC 9602](https://srv6.md/rfcs/rfc9602/)), block `5f00::/32` and node 1 = `5f00:0:1::/48` (F3216: 32-bit block, 16-bit node uSID, 16-bit function).

```junos
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block BLK0 5f00::/32
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block BLK0 local-micro-sid maximum-static-sids 2000
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 5f00:0:1::/48
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-sid block-name BLK0
```

`maximum-static-sids` reserves part of the LIB for statically configured service SIDs. By default the static LIB range is empty, so any static `micro-dt46-sid` value would fail to commit. Changing GIB/LIB sizes later is disruptive (it requires restarting routing, and dynamic SIDs can change), so size it up front. Use the same block on every router; uSID compression only works between nodes that share a block.

??? note "Classic (full-length) SIDs instead of uSID"
    ```junos
    set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator myloc 2001:db8:0:a0::/64
    set protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator myloc end-sid 2001:db8:0:a0:d01:: flavor usd
    set protocols isis interface xe-0/0/0:0.0 level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment protected locator myloc end-x-sid 2001:db8:0:a0:1a01:: flavor psp
    ```
    End and End.X SIDs must fall inside the locator prefix or the commit fails. Encapsulation defaults to a **reduced SRH**; `set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 no-reduced-srh` restores the full SRH (on ACX7000 this restarts the PFE).

## Step 3: IS-IS

```junos
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 point-to-point
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment unprotected locator LOC0 micro-adjacency-sid
set protocols isis interface lo0.0 passive
set protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-node-sid
set protocols isis level 1 disable
set protocols isis level 2 wide-metrics-only
```

- `micro-node-sid` advertises the locator and the uN SID (RFC 9352 SRv6 Locator TLV). The locator must be configured under IS-IS even if you only want SRv6 for L3VPN.
- `micro-adjacency-sid` with no value allocates a dynamic uA from the LIB. The JVD uses **unprotected** uA SIDs and relies on TI-LFA to protect uN SIDs and prefixes.
- IS-IS multi-topology (`set protocols isis topologies ipv6-unicast`) is **not** required. The JVD only uses it during migration, so IPv4 SR-MPLS and IPv6 SRv6 topologies can differ.

## Step 4: L3VPN over SRv6

On each PE, assign a service SID per VRF and enable SRv6 service signaling on the BGP families.

```junos
# VRF with a dynamic uDT46 SID (End.DT46 with NEXT-CSID)
set routing-instances CUST-A instance-type vrf
set routing-instances CUST-A interface ge-0/0/2.0
set routing-instances CUST-A route-distinguisher 192.0.2.1:100
set routing-instances CUST-A vrf-target target:65000:100
set routing-instances CUST-A protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-dt46-sid
#   or a static value from the LIB static range:  ... micro-dt46-sid 0xfc30
#   or per address family:                         ... micro-dt4-sid / micro-dt6-sid
#   classic SIDs:                                  ... locator myloc end-dt4-sid / end-dt6-sid / end-dt46-sid <sid>

# IBGP to the route reflectors (IPv6 transport)
set protocols bgp group RR type internal
set protocols bgp group RR local-address 2001:db8:ff::11
set protocols bgp group RR family inet-vpn unicast extended-nexthop
set protocols bgp group RR family inet-vpn unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet-vpn unicast accept-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6-vpn unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6-vpn unicast accept-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family route-target nexthop-resolution no-resolution
set protocols bgp group RR neighbor 2001:db8:ff::1
set protocols bgp rfc8950-compliant
set protocols bgp multipath list-nexthop
```

How it resolves: with SRv6 services enabled, Junos ignores the BGP NEXT_HOP for resolution and resolves the route on the **locator** inside the SRv6 SID, which IS-IS has installed in `inet6.3` as an `SRV6-ISIS` route. No `resolution rib` tweaks are needed. Two details matter in practice:

- `extended-nexthop` and `rfc8950-compliant` make VPN-IPv4 routes carry IPv6 next hops in the standard (RFC 8950) encoding, which matters for interoperability with other vendors.
- Route-target (RT-constraint) routes otherwise stay hidden, because the PE loopbacks exist only in `inet6.0`. `nexthop-resolution no-resolution` fixes this.

The per-VRF SID is advertised in the BGP Prefix-SID attribute (SRv6 L3 Service TLV) with the function bits transposed into the label field, as described in [RFC 9252](https://srv6.md/rfcs/rfc9252/). Inter-AS Option C works over SRv6; Option B over SRv6 is not supported. For SIDs learned only via BGP (no IGP route to the remote locator), Junos 24.2R1+ on MX can use `routing-options dynamic-tunnels  srv6`.

### Internet (Global Table) over SRv6

```junos
set protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-dt46-sid
set protocols bgp group RR family inet unicast extended-nexthop
set protocols bgp group RR family inet unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet unicast accept-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6 unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6 unicast accept-srv6-service
```

!!! warning "Filter your SID block at the border"
    The JVD filters `5f00::/16` (and more-specifics) on eBGP sessions. If another AS can inject routes covering your SID space, it can attract SRv6-encapsulated VPN traffic. See [Security](https://srv6.md/topics/security/).

## Step 5: Flex-Algo

A Flex-Algo needs a definition, IS-IS participation and **its own locator**. Services pick the algorithm through the locator their SID comes from.

```junos
# Algorithm 128 = low-latency
set routing-options flex-algorithm 128 definition metric-type delay-metric
set routing-options flex-algorithm 128 definition spf
set protocols isis source-packet-routing flex-algorithm 128

# Locator for algorithm 128, in its own /32 block
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block BLK128 5f00:a1::/32
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 5f00:a1:1::/48
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 algorithm 128
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-sid block-name BLK128
set protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-node-sid
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment unprotected locator LOC128 micro-adjacency-sid

# Option A: the whole VRF uses the low-latency locator
set routing-instances CUST-LL protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-dt46-sid

# Option B: allocate a second SID in a VRF and select it per prefix by policy
set routing-instances CUST-A protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-dt46-sid non-default
set policy-options community VOICE members 65000:911
set policy-options policy-statement LL-PREFIXES term VOICE from community VOICE
set policy-options policy-statement LL-PREFIXES term VOICE then srv6 locator LOC128 micro-dt46-sid
set policy-options policy-statement LL-PREFIXES term VOICE then accept
set protocols bgp group RR export LL-PREFIXES
```

In option B the VRF advertises its default SID for most prefixes, and the export policy on the IBGP group swaps in the algorithm-128 SID for the matching ones, so remote PEs reach those prefixes over the low-latency topology.

Delay-based algorithms need link delay: enable `delay-measurement` on the IS-IS interfaces (TWAMP Light), and advertise it as an application-specific link attribute for Flex-Algo. IS-IS installs SIDs of non-zero algorithms in `inet6color.0`. On Junos, Flex-Algo participation applies to SR-MPLS and SRv6 together — you cannot define an algorithm for SRv6 only. See [Flex-Algorithm](https://srv6.md/topics/flex-algorithm/).

## Step 6: TI-LFA and Microloop Avoidance

```junos
set protocols isis backup-spf-options use-post-convergence-lfa
set protocols isis backup-spf-options use-source-packet-routing
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 post-convergence-lfa
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 post-convergence-lfa node-protection cost 16777214
set protocols isis spf-options microloop-avoidance post-convergence-path delay 5000
```

Link protection is the default once `post-convergence-lfa` is on an interface. The JVD adds node protection with a very high cost, so the node-protecting path is preferred but a link-protecting backup is still used when no node-protecting path exists. uSID-based TI-LFA, microloop avoidance and Flex-Algo protection arrived in Junos 23.4R1. **SRLG is not considered for SRv6 TI-LFA.** The JVD measured worst-case link-failure convergence around 5 ms. See [TI-LFA](https://srv6.md/topics/ti-lfa/) for the algorithm.

## Verification

| Command | What to look for |
|---------|------------------|
| `show isis overview` | `SRv6: Enabled`, the locator and algorithm, `micro-node-SID … Flavor: PSP, USD`, post-convergence backup and microloop avoidance state |
| `show isis adjacency extensive` | `SRv6 unprotected END-X-SID …` with its flavor, per adjacency |
| `show isis database  extensive \| find SRv6` | SRv6 Locator TLV (MTID, algorithm), uN SID with block/node lengths, SRv6 MSDs, End.X SIDs |
| `show srv6 block BLK0` | GIB/LIB ranges, static and dynamic SID counts |
| `show route table inet6.3 protocol isis` | Remote locators and SIDs as `SRV6-ISIS` routes with `SRV6-Tunnel` next hops |
| `show route table inet6.0 protocol srv6` | Local service SIDs, e.g. a uDT46 SID pointing `to table CUST-A.inet.0` |
| `show route receive-protocol bgp  table CUST-A detail` | `SRv6 SID: … Behavior: 63 BL:32 NL:16 FL:16 AL:0 TL:16 TO:48` (63 = End.DT4 with NEXT-CSID) |
| `show route table CUST-A.inet.0  extensive` | `SRV6-Tunnel: Reduced-SRH Encap-mode`, the segment list and `Protocol next hop: ` |
| `show isis backup coverage` | Percentage of nodes and prefixes protected, per topology |
| `show isis backup spf results` | Backup path per destination (add `no-coverage` to list unprotected ones) |
| `ping srv6 isis ` / `traceroute srv6 isis ` | SRv6 OAM reachability of a uN or End SID |

`show spring-traffic-engineering` is for SR-TE policies, not for SRv6 locators and service SIDs.

## Limits and Gotchas

- **SID depth** (from the Junos SRv6 docs): MX encapsulates up to 6 SIDs and inserts up to 5; ACX7000 encapsulates 12 and inserts 10; PTX10002-36QDD and PTX10008 (Express 5) support 7. uSID packs up to six 16-bit uSIDs per 128-bit container, which leaves plenty of headroom for TE and TI-LFA.
- **Encap vs insert**: ingress PEs always encapsulate, so egress SIDs must support USD; transit SRH insertion for TI-LFA needs a PSP-capable last SID.
- **Static plus IS-IS SIDs**: configuring the same static uA or End.X SID under both the SRv6 manager and IS-IS fails commit (a duplicate uN is allowed; IS-IS wins).
- **IS-IS SRv6 does not support** anycast locator prefixes, SRLG, End.X interface groups or Flex-Algo locator conflict resolution.
- **No `next-hop-self` knob**: Junos IBGP needs an export policy with `then next-hop self` when you redistribute CE routes into plain IPv4/IPv6 BGP.

# SRv6 on Arista EOS: uSID Configuration and Platforms

URL: https://srv6.md/implementations/arista-eos/
Path: implementations/arista-eos.md
Summary: SRv6 uSID support on Arista EOS — uN, static uA, IS-IS, counters, SSU, and supported platforms

# SRv6 on Arista EOS

Arista EOS implements SRv6 with a **uSID-first** design: the forwarding model is built around micro-SIDs in the `F3216` format (32-bit block, 16-bit uSIDs), starting with the uN node SID and adding static uA adjacency SIDs, IS-IS integration, counters, and hitless upgrade support over the 4.35 and 4.36 release trains. The authors of OpenAI's **MRC** AI-cluster transport collaborated with Arista to implement SRv6 in EOS on Broadcom Tomahawk 5 switches, and MRC runs in large-scale production — see [AI/ML Networks](https://srv6.md/use-cases/ai-networking/).

!!! info "Source scope"
    This page summarizes Arista's public EOS user manual (EOS 4.36.2F) and the titles/summaries of Arista's public SRv6 TOI (Technical Overview of Information) listings. Full TOI documents require an Arista login; check them and the release notes for your exact version before deploying.

## Feature Timeline

| Feature | EOS release | Source |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| uN (End with uSID) | Before 4.35.2F (base support referenced by the uA TOI) | TOI listing |
| Static SRv6 adjacency segments (**uA**) | 4.35.2F | TOI: "Support for SRv6 static adjacency segments (uA)" |
| **IS-IS** SRv6 with micro-SID compression, Flex-Algo, and **TI-LFA** | 4.36.1F | TOI: "Support for SRv6 in IS-IS" |
| **Smart System Upgrade (SSU)** with SRv6 uN | 4.36.1F | TOI: "SSU support for SRv6" |
| Per-endpoint **counters** (packets/bytes per endpoint operation, e.g. uN) | 4.36.2F | TOI: "Support for SRv6 Counters" |

## Capabilities (EOS 4.36.2F user manual)

The `show srv6 capabilities` example in the user manual reports:

| Category | Supported | Not supported |
|----------|-----------|---------------|
| Endpoint behaviors | End (uN when used with uSIDs), End.DT4, End.DT6 | End.X, End.DX4, End.DX6 |
| Flavors | PSP, USD, Next-CSID | USP |
| Headend behaviors | H.Encaps | H.Encaps.Red, H.Insert, H.Insert.Red |
| uSID formats | F3216 | — |

!!! note
    Static uA support (an End.X-type adjacency micro-SID) is documented separately in the uA TOI for EOS 4.35.2F and later, so treat the capability table as a snapshot of the manual's example rather than a complete feature list.

## Supported Platforms

| Family | Models listed in the user manual |
|--------|----------------------------------|
| 7060X6 | DCS-7060X6 |
| 7280R3 / R4 | DCS-7280R3, DCS-7280R4-32\*, DCS-7280R4K-32\*, DCS-7282R4\* |
| 7500R3 | DCS-7500R3 |
| 7800R3 / R4 | DCS-7800R3, DCS-7800R4-\*, DCS-7800R4K-36PE-LC, DCS-7800R4M-36PE-LC, DCS-DL-7700R4K-\* |

On the R3/R4 (Jericho-family) platforms, SRv6 needs a TCAM profile with the `feature srv usid f3216` feature; the 7060X6 is not listed for that requirement.

## Configuration Model

The manual organizes SRv6 under `router srv6`:

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `router srv6` → `vrf default` | SRv6 configuration context |
| `micro-segment domain` → `block`, `usid length`, `gib range` | Defines the uSID block, uSID length, and Global ID Block range |
| `locator` → `prefix micro-segment domain  end usid ` | Allocates the node's uN from the domain |
| `igp algorithm flex-algo ` | Associates a locator with a Flex-Algo |
| `show srv6 capabilities` / `domain` / `locator` / `routes` | Verification |
| `ping srv6 sid … via segment-list …`, `traceroute srv6 sid …` | SRv6 OAM |

See the user manual for complete configuration examples; exact syntax varies between EOS releases.

!!! warning "OAM gotcha"
    The manual notes that the target uN prefix (for example the /48) must be configured on a loopback for `ping srv6` / `traceroute srv6` to that uN to work.

## Where It Fits

- **AI back-end fabrics** — static, source-routed uSID paths on Tomahawk 5 (7060X6 class) are what MRC uses; see [AI/ML Networks](https://srv6.md/use-cases/ai-networking/) and [CLOS & Load Balancing](https://srv6.md/topics/clos-glb/).
- **DC/WAN edge and spine** — Jericho-based 7280R3/R4 and 7500R3/7800R3/R4 for uSID with IS-IS, Flex-Algo and TI-LFA.

## Further Reading

- [Implementations Overview](https://srv6.md/implementations/)
- [MRC and SRv6](https://srv6.md/ai/mrc/) - EOS on Tomahawk 5 in OpenAI's and Microsoft's SRv6 AI fabrics
- [uSID Compression](https://srv6.md/topics/usid-compression/) - F3216 format and shift-and-forward
- [AI/ML Networks](https://srv6.md/use-cases/ai-networking/) - MRC: OpenAI's SRv6 static source routing in production
- [TI-LFA](https://srv6.md/topics/ti-lfa/) - Fast reroute with SRv6 repair segments
